verses.text: Elisha said, "Listen to the LORD's word. This is what the LORD says: 'About this time tomorrow, at the gate of Samaria, seven litres of fine flour will sell for just one piece of silver, and fourteen litres of barley will sell for one piece of silver.'"

The officer whose arm the king leaned on said to the man of God, "Even if the LORD opened windows in the sky, could this happen?" Elisha answered, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
Four men with leprosy were sitting at the entrance of the city gate. They said to each other, "Why should we sit here until we die?

If we say, 'Let's go into the city,' we will die there, because there is a famine in the city. And if we stay here, we will die too. So let's go over to the Syrian army and give ourselves up. If they spare us, we will live. If they kill us, we were going to die anyway."
So at dusk they got up and went to the Syrian camp. When they reached the edge of the camp, there was no one there.

The Lord had made the Syrian army hear the sound of chariots and horses, the noise of a great army. They had said to each other, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us!"
So they had got up and run away at dusk. They left their tents, their horses, and their donkeys. They left the camp just as it was and ran for their lives.

When the men with leprosy reached the edge of the camp, they went into one tent and ate and drank. They took silver, gold, and clothes from it and went and hid them. Then they came back, went into another tent, took things from it too, and hid them.

Then they said to each other, "What we are doing is not right. Today is a day of good news, and we are keeping it to ourselves. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go right now and tell the king's palace."

So they went and called out to the gatekeepers of the city. They told them, "We went into the Syrian camp, and there was no one there, not a sound of anyone. There were only horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents left just as they were."
The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported inside the king's palace.

The king got up in the night and said to his officers, "I will tell you what the Syrians have done. They know we are starving. So they have left the camp to hide in the countryside. They are thinking, 'When the Israelites come out of the city, we will capture them alive and get into the city.'"

One of his officers answered, "Let some men take five of the horses that are still left in the city. If they die, they will be no worse off than all the other Israelites who are left here, or all those who have already died. Let's send them to see what happened."
So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Syrian army. He told them, "Go and find out."

They followed the Syrians as far as the Jordan River. The whole road was covered with clothes and equipment the Syrians had thrown away as they ran in a hurry. The messengers came back and told the king.

Then the people went out and took everything from the Syrian camp. So seven litres of fine flour sold for one piece of silver, and fourteen litres of barley sold for one piece of silver, just as the LORD had said.
The king had put the officer whose arm he leaned on in charge of the gate. But the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to see him.

It happened just as the man of God had told the king: "About this time tomorrow, at the gate of Samaria, fourteen litres of barley will sell for one piece of silver, and seven litres of fine flour will sell for one piece of silver."

And the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD opened windows in the sky, could this happen?" And Elisha had said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
That is exactly what happened to him. The people trampled him in the gateway, and he died.
